citation.title: European Industry and the EU's Climate Policy 2024-29
citation.venue_or_publisher: InfluenceMap (LobbyMap platform briefing), web page; Executive Summary dated May 2025

question: How corporate and industry-association climate policy engagement in the EU shifted between 2019 and 2025, and how industry advocacy (competitiveness narratives) is shaping the EU climate agenda for 2024-2029.
data: LobbyMap platform: nearly 200 non-financial companies domiciled in 'EU plus' and 80 industry associations (platform covers over 1000 companies and 330 associations); a review of over 20 industry-association pre-election policy papers (July 2023 to May 2024); scores for 25 key associations, 2019 and 2025. Does not use participant lists or COP delegations.
method: Evidence of policy engagement is tracked in near real time from public sources and scored against government policy benchmarks and IPCC-based science benchmarks for 1.5C; entities get performance bands (A to E) and a share 'science-aligned' or 'misaligned'. Narratives in association policy papers are coded into three common arguments and compared with IPCC guidance. Detailed scoring rules are on external LobbyMap methodology pages, not in this page.

definitions.definition: An entity's positions on and efforts to influence climate policy align with the scientific consensus needed for the Paris temperature goals.
definitions.quote: Science-Aligned Climate Policy Engagement is where an entity's positions on and efforts to influence climate-related government policy align with the global scientific consensus

definitions.definition: Based on the 2013 UN Guide for Responsible Corporate Engagement in Climate Policy; covers engagement with measures issued by mandated bodies to cut GHG emissions; excludes financial-system rules such as CSRD.
definitions.quote: The LobbyMap methodology uses a definition of policy engagement based on the 2013 UN Guide for Responsible Corporate Engagement in Climate Policy.

definitions.definition: Non-financial entities with legal domicile in EU plus; excludes US companies with large European operations and 'reverse headquarters' companies.
definitions.quote: The companies covered are non-financial entities with legal domicile in "EU plus" (EU Members and the UK, Norway, Iceland, Switzerland, and Liechtenstein).

definitions.definition: Industry associations adopt the positions of a small, most vocal share of members, often from the fossil fuel value chain.
definitions.quote: industry associations are drawn towards the positions of a small proportion of their members (often from the fossil fuel value chain)

proxies.indicator: LobbyMap score against government and IPCC-based benchmarks, from publicly available data sources; banded A to E
proxies.quote: Evidence of corporate and industry association policy engagement is tracked in near real time across a range of publicly available data sources and scored against authoritative and external benchmarks

proxies.indicator: Each of 25 key associations is labelled with a sector (e.g. Energy, Chemicals, Cross-sector, Metals & Mining, Utilities); how sectors were assigned is not explained
proxies.page: How Europe's Key Industry Associations Compare on Climate Policy Engagement (table)

proxies.indicator: Content of pre-election policy papers coded for three tactics: competitiveness framing, carrots over regulation, vague terminology
proxies.quote: Analysis of over 20 pre-election policy papers from industry associations previously found to be resistant to EU climate policy ambition identified three common arguments or tactics
proxies.page: Industry's Efforts to Shape the Climate Policy Narrative in Europe

findings.claim: Share of European companies with science-aligned or partially aligned engagement rose from 24% to 52%; misaligned fell from 34% to 13%.
findings.quote: 52% of European companies tracked by the platform now demonstrate science-aligned or partially science-aligned climate policy engagement

findings.claim: Cross-sector business federations (BusinessEurope, MEDEF, CEOE, Confindustria, BDI) are among the most negative voices, despite members that are more supportive.
findings.quote: are some of the most negative voices on climate policy in the region
findings.page: Corporate Climate Policy Engagement in the EU from 2019-2025

findings.claim: Aligned industry associations rose from 2% to 12% (2019 to 2025), slower than companies.
findings.quote: aligned entities increasing from 2% to 12% between 2019 and 2025
findings.page: Corporate Climate Policy Engagement in the EU from 2019-2025

findings.claim: Energy-sector associations Eurogas and FuelsEurope are scored D+ and D in 2025 in the key-association table (fossil-linked associations are not labelled as such by the source).
findings.page: How Europe's Key Industry Associations Compare on Climate Policy Engagement (table)

findings.claim: Industry narratives are judged to have influenced the Commission's Competitiveness Compass and Clean Industrial Deal.
findings.quote: the industry narratives identified in this briefing are playing a significant role in shaping the climate policy agenda for the next EU legislative cycle
findings.page: The Impact on the EU's Climate Policy Agenda So Far

limitations.point: Sample limited to non-financial companies domiciled in EU plus; excludes US companies with big European operations and reverse-headquarters firms; financial-sector and CSRD-type engagement excluded.
limitations.quote: It does not include US companies with significant European operations nor does it include "reverse headquarters" companies

limitations.point: No definition of 'fossil fuel' company or fossil-linked association; fossil link is mentioned only in passing. Nothing on delegations, badges, COP participant lists, conflicts of interest or undue influence.
Scoring methodology and sector assignment are on external LobbyMap pages (not in this text); no validation or error rate is reported here.

Author is an advocacy-oriented think tank; the page is a briefing, not peer reviewed. Several charts/figures and the tactic lists appear not to have been extracted (e.g. 'identified three common arguments or tactics:' is followed by no list in the text).
